name: Telemetryx
positioning: Consolidation play. Sells 'one bill instead of four' to platform leadership.

pages.title: Telemetryx — Plans
pages.text: Telemetryx bundles logs, metrics, traces and product analytics into a single platform fee starting at $2,400/month, plus consumption. Product analytics is not sold standalone — it is an add-on to the observability platform. Seats are included but capped by role: viewer seats are unlimited, builder seats are $40/month each. Contracts are annual with a 20% uplift for month-to-month. Retention is 13 months across all data types.

pages.title: Telemetryx Docs — Getting started
pages.text: Telemetryx ingests via the OpenTelemetry collector; there is no proprietary SDK for web analytics, so browser events require a custom OTel web bridge that the team maintains as a community project. Expect a multi-week setup for product analytics specifically. Server-side is first-class.

pages.title: Telemetryx Docs — Quotas
pages.text: No documented per-second ingestion cap; throughput is governed by your consumption contract. Warehouse sync is real-time via the streaming export. SSO, SCIM, and audit logs are included at every tier. The primary constraint customers report is cost predictability rather than technical limits.

pricing.notes: Builder seats $40/mo, annual contract, analytics is an add-on

reviews.quote: One vendor instead of four genuinely simplified our life, and governance is best in class. But nobody on the team can predict next month's bill within 30%.
We bought it for observability and inherited the analytics. Product managers never adopted it — the OTel web bridge was too fragile to trust.
Strong consolidation story for platform leadership. Weak self-serve motion; expect professional services.

changelog.entry: OTel web bridge moved to community maintenance
